items.text: REFERRED TO CRIME VICTIMS, CRIME AND CORRECTION

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4614

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to reform of urban
correctional facilities


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This bill, sets forth legislative findings that smaller correctional
facilities are more secure and better able to serve their public
purpose than larger, overcrowded facilities. The bill accordingly
limits the current population on Rikers Island in the City of New York
to its present numbers, and requires the State Commission of
Correction to develop a plan to reduce the population of Rikers Island
to the population in residence on January 1, 1970.

 PROVISIONS :
Section 1 of the bill is a statement of legislative intent, finding
that the size of local correctional facilities plays an important role
in the safety and security of such facilities, the services which can
be provided by such facilities and the cost of providing them. The
statement continues to take notice of the conditions of overcrowding
which exist in the various correctional facilities run by the City of
New York on Rikers Island. Since it would be prohibitively expensive
to upgrade these facilities, the bill announces a legislative intent
to cap the current population of Rikers Island and to direct the State
Commission of Correction to develop a plan to reduce the population in
these facilities.

Section 2 of the bill adds a new section 45-a to the Correction Law,
which prohibits the State Commission of Correction from approving any
plans or specifications for new construction on Rikers Island, and
from increasing or waiving the maximum prisoners capacity, or taking
another action which would permit the number of prisoners in Rikers
Island facilities from exceeding the number in residence on July 1st,
1983.  Section 45-a further provides that the Commission shall
establish a plan for the orderly reduction of inmate space on Rikers
Island, in favor of smaller new or renovated correctional facilities
in other parts of the city. Subject to the availability of such
alternative placements, the plan is to provide for a reduction by 1992
to the population levels in existence in 1970.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The various local correctional facilities on Rikers Island are
currently under population caps imposed by federal judges due to
overcrowding, poor sanitation, and other facility shortcomings. The
current population of all facilities on Rikers Island is over 8,000
inmates many of whom are housed in temporary quarters in areas never
designed or intended as detention space. The NYC Commissioner of
Correction has noted that "the age and decrepit condition" of the
House of Detention for Men on Rikers Island make it difficult for the
city to meet mandated standards, and the City of New York has also
found that it would be prohibitively expensive to upgrade this
facility. The other correctional and detention facilities on Rikers
Island share this plight.

Large, overcrowded facilities such as those on Rikers Island do not
preserve the safety of inmates, correctional officers, or the public,
and they do not carry out the public purposes for which they operate.
Neither humane housing of those which awaiting trial on criminal
charges nor rehabilitation of sentenced misdemeanants is achievable in
these facilities. These problems are compounded by the enormous costs
of transportation caused by the geographic remoteness of Rikers Island
from courts and other processing points.


The City of New York has already launched an ambitious program of
capital construction of correctional space. This legislation would
assist this program by encouraging the transfer of inmates currently
housed on Rikers Island to new or renovated facilities, by involving
the State Commission of Correction in the planning process for such
facilities at an earlier date, and by preventing the expenditure of
public funds on correctional facilities on Rikers Island whose
rehabilitation is not cost-effective.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
1989-08-Referred to Crime and Correction Committee.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
180th day after enactment.

summary: Prohibits new correctional facilities on Rikers Island in NYC from increasing prisoner capacity in excess of maximum established on 7/1/87; requires board of correction and NYC department of correction to develop plan for orderly reduction of Rikers Island prisoner population by transferring of prisoners from Rikers Island to smaller new or renovated correctional facilities by 1/1/14; provides that any municipal official not complying herewith shall be issued a citation.
title: Mandates reform of Rikers Island correctional facilities and orderly reduction of prisoner population
